exposure: Prolonged rupture of the membrane (>24 h)
cohort: The study included 260 postpartum women (65 cases diagnosed with puerperal sepsis and 195 controls free from puerperal sepsis) attending public hospitals in the Dawro Zone, Southwest Ethiopia.
finding: Rural residence, lack of formal education, no ANC, prolonged rupture of membranes, home deliveries, frequent vaginal examinations, and cesarean section were significantly associated with an increased risk of puerperal sepsis.
mod_finding: Home delivery and cesarean section were identified as significant risk factors for puerperal sepsis.
followup_time: Up to 42 days postpartum (as per the definition of puerperal sepsis)
